rows.text: In Edwards v Pohiva (Court of Appeal, Burchett and Tompkins JJ and Ward CJ, Appeal 1/2003, C 559/1998, judgment 25 July 2003) the court states that after Parliament's contempt hearing of Thursday 19 September 1996 'The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly issued a warrant', dated 20 September 1996 and addressed to the Minister of Police, which it quotes as signed 'Fusitu'a / Chairman of the Legislative Assembly'; the warrant was executed on 20 September 1996, the day it was issued.
rows.locator: [2003] Tonga LR 231 (case header, PDF page 231); 234-235, paragraphs [5]-[8] (PDF pages 234-235)
rows.uncertainty: The signature block reads 'Chairman of the Legislative Assembly' (the Tongan 'Sea'); the court calls the issuer the Speaker. The source names him only by his noble title. An 11 September 1996 summons by 'the Chairman of the Legislative Assembly' is recited without a name. No appointment date. The damages litigation is not imported.

bounded_scope: Speaker observations for CLAUDE-C01-24 only (role to_speaker on the to_legislative_assembly observation). Royal appointment, the Assembly's election or recommendation of its Speaker, the oath, a resignation, a revocation, an acting or interim Speaker and a Deputy Speaker presiding stay separate rows; holder observations are decided in the packet, not by any row.
